messages:
violet: Quick heads-up: while prepping the 0.7.1 gem release I hit a puzzling CI flake on linux-musl matrix. Native extension build passes but spec auth_retry_spec.rb intermittently fails with 401 on first try then passes on retry. Haven't seen this locally. Anyone seen something like that?

ben: That's odd. Which native extension are we shipping? The ffi-based fast serializer? Could memory layout differences cause header mutation across threads?

violet: It's the new C extension for token cache (ext/token_cache). The test uses a mocked token rotation that writes a new token to the cache, then calls the client. Failure is that the first request after rotation gets 401 about 1/10 runs.

tara: Two quick hypotheses: 1) the C ext exposes a pointer to a string that gets freed/reused leading to stale Authorization header if we convert lazily, 2) the HTTP adapter might be reusing an underlying socket with old header metadata.

ben: Can you paste the minimal failing test snippet?

violet: Sure:```ruby
it 'applies refreshed token for next request' do
  token_cache.write('tmp-token')
  client = Redwood::Client.new(token: token_cache.read)
  token_cache.write('rotated')
  res1 = client.chat.generate(prompt: 'x')
  expect(res1.status).to eq(200)
end
```

ben: Ah, client is created before rotation so it will hold any in-memory headers. We rely on token_cache notifying the client in prod via callback. Tests assume passive sync.

tara: Two fixes: update test to call client.refresh_from_cache or change client to read-per-request in test-only mode. But for root cause we should audit C ext for returning fresh Ruby String objects each time (use rb_str_new_cstr) not a static pointer.

violet: I'll inspect the ext code. Meanwhile can we gate the gem release until we confirm it's not a memory-safety risk? The flake is small but concerning.

ben: Also saw a warning in build logs: "string not copied to Ruby object" from valgrind on alpine. That suggests the C ext was returning pointer to stack memory. If true we must fix before releasing.

ci-bot: github/actions - ruby-sdk CI #3304 triggered by violet - jobs: unit, integration (linux-musl), lint

tara: Plan: 1) add a tiny test that forks a process to simulate binstub/fork behavior and writes new token after fork; 2) modify token_cache ext to always copy token into a new Ruby string; 3) add a client method `refresh_token!` that invalidates internal header cache and resets http pool.

violet: I'll open a draft PR with the ext fix + the refresh_token! API and a changelog note. For backwards compat the refresh is no-op unless user calls it.

ben: If we add refresh_token!, can we wire the sampleapp to call it on SIGHUP so devs see a safe pattern?

violet: Good idea for sampleapp docs. Also adding ENV RB_TOKEN_REFRESH_MODE=per_request for quickstart so contributors don't hit this.

release-bot: Blocking release 0.7.1 until CI passes and native ext memory warnings addressed.

ben: OK locking the release makes sense. I'll review the draft PR once it's up. If tests pass we can unblock and do a patch release.

violet: Thanks all, pushing a small fix now and will ping here when CI green.
